ELI5 - What is a warrant canary and how does it work?

It's like a dead man's switch; a passive countermeasure. If you get a warrant accompanied by a gag order, you are not allowed to tell anyone you have been served. However, as long as you have not been served such a warrant, you are free to tell anyone that you have not yet been served. So you keep repeating "No warrant has been served at this time" at regular intervals. The moment you do get a warrant, you may not tell anyone you've been served. However, you are under no obligation to keep saying you have not been served, thus you stop updating the "canary". This way, your inaction will inform your users that a warrant has been served without you violating the gag order.

I'm not sure about the legal standing of such a canary; they may be able to charge you with something regardless. But the fact that it's even necessary should be cause for concern.

Back in the olden days, miners used to carry canaries into the mines as a safety precaution against invisible poisonous gas build up. As they had smaller bodies (the canaries, not the miners), they would stop singing/faint/die when the gas started building up, but before the miners were in serious danger.

Miners would check the status of the canary periodically, and if it had croaked/stopped singing, would get out of there sharpish.

The idea of a warrant canary is similar, but a little different. The basis is, in this context, that the canary will stop singing if it is not looked after regularly. So if a secret order is taken against a site, preventing them from telling the users that they are being investigated, they will stop "feeding" the canary, and it will stop singing. It could be something as simple as a text file with today's date on it which the site admin updates every day; As soon as the file does not contain the days date, that means something has happened.

Of course, investigations now also demand that any canaries are serviced/fed, so the actual usefulness is debatable.

Wait.... so the warrants can now force an admin/operator to update their canaries? Has this been tested in court yet?

I get the whole gag order thing, but something doesn't smell right about forcing an entity to DO something, rather than preventing them from doing another.

A canary, by the strictest definition of the law, is perfectly legal. in and of itself, the canary mechanism does not technically reveal that a warrant has been served. It only tells users that "up to this point" no warrant has been served.

I think a prosecutor would have a tough time proving that particular negative.

From my limited knowledge, it comes from prosecutions where laws and rights are shuffled around in a grey area; In the territory of "Sure, you can stop servicing any canaries you use, but we suspect that it would not help your case".

It would come down to the canary operator, deciding if they were willing to potentially be charged with subversion.
The use of a canary is not so much to protect the site owner, but the users. It serves as a warning that data is no longer protected.
